result_text:
A `SyntaxError` in a test module you name explicitly is no longer swallowed. Running green on a broken module now raises an `ImportError` that includes the full `SyntaxError` traceback, like `unittest` does. I only ran your MWE by hand: `python -m green tests.test_my` now shows the error instead of "No Tests Found". I didn't run the project's test suite.

The cause was in `loadTarget` in `green/loader.py`. When it loaded the dotted name `tests.test_my`, any exception was caught, logged to debug, and ignored. A `SyntaxError` isn't an `ImportError`, so `unittest` let it through and green discarded it. The later file-path fallback didn't apply because `tests.test_my` isn't a file path, so nothing was found.

The fix catches `SyntaxError` on that path and returns a failing test that carries the traceback. I moved the existing "Failed to import" message-building code into a shared helper, `_importFailure`, so both paths use it.

The error currently comes out as an uncaught traceback ending in `ImportError: Failed to import "tests.test_my"`, because the failing test is invoked while green builds its target list. That is the same way it already reports import failures when you name a file by path.
